meta.gift: memory, tide, and the salt that keeps names from dissolving
meta.waning: the tide recedes from the world's edges; memories thin and the drowned begin to speak
meta.curse_desc: salt blooms beneath the skin; the afflicted forget faces first, then their own
veils: The drownings are not offerings. They are silencings — of what the drowned heard in the tide.
The Radiance never drowned — it was drowned, by the very powers that now pray for its return.
They drowned it in mercy, at its own asking: it had begun to remember the world before this one, and memory is contagious.
meta.epigraph: The tide gives, and the tide is given to; what remains to us are the keepings, and each was kept by a hand that loved only its own account. Read them against one another, pilgrim, for no single telling was ever meant to hold.

ages.name: the Age of the Gift
ages.blurb: the Drowned Radiance gave the world memory, tide, and the salt that keeps names from dissolving.

ages.name: the Age of Names
ages.blurb: The powers withdrew to their high seats and mortals learned to matter.

ages.name: the Age of Dusk
ages.blurb: The present age. What remains keeps the roads, and pilgrims walk toward rumours of a cure.

e1.text: the Drowned Radiance rose (or was raised — the tellings differ) and gave the world memory, tide, and the salt that keeps names from dissolving.

e2.text: Ysengar, god of the hunt and the mercy of endings, claimed a portion of the gift and took a throne.

e4.text: The Salt of Ysengar was wrought as regalia of Ysengar's throne.

e5.text: Olanwyn, god of harvest, plenty, and the debt of plenty, claimed a portion of the gift and took a throne.

e6.text: Mazorrion, god of storms and unkept promises, claimed a portion of the gift and took a throne.

e8.text: The Tide of Olanwyn was wrought as regalia of Olanwyn's throne.

e9.text: Draehild, the Still Water, rose against the thrones. Ysengar led the powers to war.
e9.hidden: Mazorrion treated with Draehild in secret and was spared what followed.

e10.text: Draehild and Ysengar destroyed one another at the war's end. Neither throne nor grave was left to either.
e10.hidden: Ysengar chose it, knowing the cost.

e11.text: Velanoth, god of war and the keeping of thresholds, claimed a portion of the gift and took a throne.

e12.text: Mazorrion and Velanoth fell to war over a single domain. Velanoth kept it; Mazorrion was cast down and is named in no liturgy since.
e12.hidden: The domain was never Velanoth's to keep.

e14.text: The Conch of Velanoth was wrought as regalia of Velanoth's throne.

e15.text: The waning began: the tide recedes from the world's edges; memories thin and the drowned begin to speak. Mortals called the affliction the Brine-hollowing: salt blooms beneath the skin; the afflicted forget faces first, then their own.

e16.text: The Church of Olanwyn was raised at Syliagarhold; Fenach of the Last Door took its first pulpit, preaching that the waning is a trial and the faithful will be spared.

e17.text: Vereneth of the Last Door was cast out of Verulisspire and founded the Cult of the Open Door, teaching that the powers above themselves caused the waning.
e17.hidden: The heresy is nearer the truth than the sermon.

e18.text: Isheneth the Lantern-eyed, sword-hand of Velanoth, opened the gates of Atherichold to the Cult of the Open Door over a grievance no chronicle agrees on.
e18.hidden: Isheneth acted on a promise from the Cult of the Open Door: that the marked of their house would be spared the Brine-hollowing. The promise was not kept.

e19.text: At the urging of Fenach, the saint Omennoth of the Last Door was given to the Drowned Radiance in the rite of restoration. For a generation, the waning slowed.
e19.hidden: The rite did not restore anything. It only fed the waning more slowly — and Fenach suspected as much.

e20.text: Iriaulaspire fell. Velanoth, god of war and the keeping of thresholds, died at the foot of their own throne; the crown was carried away and never worn again.

e21.text: Isheneth was found bearing the Brine-hollowing, and was not spared.

e22.text: Ranmoth the Quiet founded the Order of the Brine at Hestiaynevault, sworn to stand against the Brine-hollowing.

e23.text: At the urging of Fenach, the saint Yoransila the Lantern-eyed was given to the Drowned Radiance in the rite of restoration. For a generation, the waning slowed.
e23.hidden: The rite did not restore anything. It only fed the waning more slowly — and Fenach suspected as much.

e24.text: Galulwyn the Grey united the river-clans and was crowned in Oloastreach; the realm took the name Belotthollow.

e25.text: For thirty years the waning simply stopped. Orchards bore, the marked recovered, and it was called a mercy. Then it resumed, exactly where it had left off.
e25.hidden: Something was being paid during those thirty years, and the payments were recorded nowhere.

e26.text: Quelidane the Kindly united the river-clans and was crowned in Athrioncrown; the realm took the name Kawyngate.

e27.text: Irric of the Empty Scabbard, last-sworn of the Order of the Brine, set out for the deep roads, where the affliction is said to begin, carrying the order's final blessing.

e28.text: Word came that Irric fell to the marked, and then word came that Irric led them. The order believes neither.

e29.text: Olanwyn, god of harvest, plenty, and the debt of plenty, was unmade upon their own throne. No wound was found, and no successor dared the seat.
e29.hidden: What unmade them was not violence but understanding — a truth arrived at, all at once.

e30.text: Ysulmund the Quiet came to the ruin of Atherichold bearing a claim to Iriaulaspire, and was neither crowned nor turned away.
e30.hidden: The claim is false, and Ysulmund knows it.

e31.text: The afflicted stopped hiding. They keep the wayhouses now, and take no toll from those already bearing the Brine-hollowing.
e31.hidden: Among them are some who were never afflicted at all.

a1.description: Regalia of the throne of Ysengar, borne since the church first rose at Ghalorncrown. The hunt-god took a portion of the gift and named endings a mercy. It is written that the salt within keeps a name from dissolving, and that the faithful who suffer are only tried. That the god was unmade at the war's end the tellings do not deny — yet a trial, the church holds, is never a bill.
a1.placement: Kept long at Ghalorncrown, and then kept poorly.

a2.description: Regalia of Olanwyn's throne, wrought in the vault's first year. Harvest-god, plenty-god, keeper of the debt that plenty owes. The royal line of Fenanastshroud bore this tide through every season and names itself blameless in all that came after. Olanwyn was unmade upon the very seat, without wound and without heir. Of the debt, the courtiers say nothing at all.

a3.name: Ysengar's War-Pearl
knowledge: (year 149) Draehild, the Still Water, rose against the thrones. Ysengar led the powers to war.
Ysengar, god of the hunt and the mercy of endings: fate — unmade at the war's end (year 160).

a3.description: A pearl, they'll swear to you, plucked whole from the god's own war. When the Still Water — Draehild, was it? — rose against the high thrones, Ysengar led the powers down to meet it. A great matter, and the pearl recalls most of it, or near enough. The hunt-god did not come home from that war; that much every teller grants, though the years they give never quite align.
a3.placement: Dug from the old battle-earth near Ghalorncrown.

Velanoth was slain at the foot of the seat — by the heretic hordes of the Open Door, some insist, though no blade is named. A god of thresholds, cut down upon his own. The realm keeps its innocence, and the true hand its silence.

The liturgy names Velanoth's hand at the drowning and calls the loss a trial. A trial, it holds, and never a bill.

a7.description: The crown of Iriaulaspire, carried out from Atherichold and never again worn. When the kingdom fell, Velanoth died at the throne's foot — or so the enemy would have it. The court holds otherwise: that the threshold-god withdrew, and waits yet in some hidden seat for the crown to be brought home. No head has dared it since. A kingdom does not fall, the courtiers say, while its god still breathes.
a7.placement: Found at the foot of a throne in Iriaulaspire, beneath the dust of the banners.

a8.description: A blade said once to have been Isheneth's, the Lantern-eyed. The court remembers a loyal sword, and sets the fall of Iriaulaspire back in the Age of the Gift, ages before it truly came. Velanoth died at the throne's foot; the crown went out and stayed out. Of what the drowned are given to, the courtiers keep a careful quiet — the tide, they allow, takes more than lives, and holds its silence over all it hears beneath.

a9.description: A conch borne by Saint Yoransila, the Lantern-eyed. Freely given to the church, the tellings hold, and freely the saint gave herself — down into the Radiance at Fenach's word, that the waning might slow a generation more. So it did. The faithful account it grace, and the relic grace twice over: a gift, and the gift of one who did not flinch. Suffering is a trial. The church has always taught so.

Irric went to the deep roads where the affliction is said to begin, bearing the order's final blessing — an age gone now, by the older reckonings. Word came that Irric fell to the marked. Then word came that Irric led them. The order believes neither, and keeps the vigil it swore, miracles be hanged.

Fell to the marked, or led them — the order holds to neither rumour. It holds instead to the oath, and to the plain fact that a vigil kept is never a vigil wasted, whatever the tide withdraws.

The court of Fenanastshroud grieves a sovereign taken without cause or crime, and lays no fault at the realm's door. The debt of plenty, the courtiers do not raise. Some seats, once emptied, are simply left.
a13.placement: Taken from a throne room at Fenanastshroud where nothing else was disturbed.

a14.description: The writ by which Ysulmund the Quiet laid claim to Iriaulaspire. Bestowed, the court would say, and never taken — a lawful grant borne to the ruin of Atherichold, where the claimant was neither crowned nor cast out. The line endures, the courtiers insist. Yet the deep tide keeps its own ledger, and holds in silence all that the drowned once heard; a claim to a throne is a small thing beside it.
a14.placement: Found where it was abandoned, at Atherichold.

a15.description: A draught poured free at the wayhouses, for those already marked. The afflicted keep the roads now — stopped their hiding, bless them, and take no toll from any who bear the salt beneath the skin. Drink deep, friend. Though between you and me, not every hand that pours is a salted one; some among them, I'd wager, never hollowed at all. Who's to say, on roads this long?
a15.placement: Bought from a peddler working the roads near the Pilgrim Roads.
